claims.text: WC particles and a minor Nb addition can be incorporated into a CoCrFeNi coating by laser cladding.
Nb reacts with WC during laser cladding to form NbC in situ.
The modified coating also contains carbide phases such as Cr3C2 and residual WC.
Nb promotes WC dissolution and improves the uniformity of particle distribution in the CoCrFeNi coating.
NbC and the other carbide phases will be uniformly distributed throughout the modified alloy.
The in situ carbide phases are thermally stable through sliding temperatures as high as 800 °C.
The carbide phases act as self-adaptive, lubricious barriers during sliding.
The carbide phases resist deformation and reduce hard-phase delamination under sliding stress.
The carbide phases reduce dislocation activity and stress concentrations in the CoCrFeNi coating.
The lubricant-like action of the carbides remains effective from room temperature through 800 °C.
The WC- and Nb-modified coating will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The wear-rate improvement will persist across the entire range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The WC- and Nb-modified coating will have a lower average coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire temperature range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi suffers increased elevated-temperature friction and wear because of phase instabilities and the absence of lubricious reinforcement.
The intervention will remain effective at contact pressures near 0.9 GPa.
Low friction at approximately 0.936 GPa has been demonstrated for a two-dimensional (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 material under ambient conditions.
In situ NbC formation and improved wear resistance have been demonstrated in a laser-cladded WC/Nb-modified CoCrFeNi coating.
The modified coating's tribological performance and phase stability specifically at 800 °C remain unvalidated by the cited evidence.
